title: From audit findings to proven fixes
course_title: Search Engine Optimization (SEO): Professional Audits and Client Practice

say: From audit findings to proven fixes.
This is the video for module two of the professional SEO course.
Amateurs hand a client a long list of everything imperfect. Professionals hand over a short, ordered plan where the first items clearly matter most.

say: Start with Search Console. URL Inspection shows whether a page is on Google, which canonical Google chose, and a live test of the page now.

say: The free Screaming Frog crawler checks up to 500 URLs on a laptop, and finds broken links, redirects, titles and canonicals. On small hosting, lower the crawl speed, and only crawl sites you have permission to audit.

say: Give each finding three scores from 1 to 5. Impact is how much it could change visibility or sales for pages the business cares about.

panel.heading: Score with Impact x Confidence x Ease
items: Impact: how much it could change results
Confidence: how sure the evidence makes you
Ease: how easy it is to do (5 is very easy)
Multiply them. The maximum is 125

say: Confidence is how sure you are, from evidence, that fixing it will help.

say: Multiply them. For example, Ada found the homepage canonical pointing to an old staging domain. Five times five times five, 125. Her slow pages scored only 18, because they need a developer and more time.

say: But some issues stop a site appearing at all. A sitewide noindex, a robots.txt that blocks everything, or canonicals to an old domain. These are critical. Report them the same day.

panel.heading: Score with Impact x Confidence x Ease
items: Impact: how much it could change results
Confidence: how sure the evidence makes you
Ease: how easy it is to do (5 is very easy)
Multiply them. The maximum is 125
panel.rule: Critical blockers, like a stray noindex, go first, whatever the score.

say: A finding explains a problem. A ticket tells one person exactly what to do. It can live in a WhatsApp group or a shared sheet.
Ada's ticket for 38 tour pages with the same title included all 38 new titles, written by her. Vague tickets like improve titles are the most common reason SEO advice never gets done.

panel.heading: A ticket a developer can finish alone
items: A short title naming the change
The affected URLs or template
Current state and required state
Acceptance criteria: the check that proves it
Priority and owner

say: A recommendation is not a result. First, open the page source and confirm the change. If it does not show, ask the developer to clear the cache before you call it failed.

panel.heading: Three checks that a fix is live

cards.d: View source on two or three affected pages, on a phone too, and confirm the exact change.
Crawl with the same settings as your baseline and compare the counts.
Test live URL in URL Inspection, and click Validate fix for indexing issues.

say: Second, recrawl with the same settings and compare counts.

say: Third, check Google's view with URL Inspection. Validation typically takes up to about two weeks.

say: Chioma rewrote titles on 8 recipe pages of a food blog. She compared equal periods, 28 days before and 28 days after, and left out the week of the change.

Check seasonality and Google updates

say: To remember. Triage by what matters to the business. Fix critical blockers first, then score the rest. Write tickets with clear acceptance criteria. Verify every fix three ways. And measure with equal periods, a comparison group and a dated change log.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Triage by business importance, not raw counts
Critical blockers first, then score the rest
Tickets state current, required and acceptance
Verify every fix three ways
Equal periods, a comparison group, a change log
